paper.title: Can Large Language Models Invent Algorithms to Improve Themselves?: Algorithm Discovery for Recursive Self-Improvement through Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: Self-Developing lets a seed LLM generate model-improvement (merging) algorithms as code, score them by merging and evaluating, and DPO-train itself (the algorithm factory) on the results; discovered algorithms beat human-designed merging on GSM8k and transfer to new candidate models.

evidence.support_explanation: Search budget 3 × 3000 samples (100–300 executable per iteration).

evidence.support_explanation: Baseline grid is coarse (3 ratios per candidate).

evidence.quote: We apply the top 15 algorithms discovered by the algorithm factory (based on their performance on the development set with the original candidate models) to these new models.
evidence.support_explanation: Transfer protocol: retained merge code applied to new candidates without re-optimisation.

evidence.support_explanation: Both persistent changes of the system are weights: the factory (LoRA-DPO) and the merged model. The retained Python merge function is a weight-space operator whose only use is producing new weights; it is not a prompt, skill, tool, workflow, memory, evaluator or configuration of a deployed agent.

Searched §3–4 and App. A–F: no equal-budget untrained-factory or random/evolutionary search arm, single run, no intervals; algorithm A reduces to 0.25·tau_1 plus broadcast means of the other task vectors, a point outside the 20/40/60% Task Arithmetic grid.

signatures.object: Algorithm factory LLM (weights, LoRA-DPO) and its generated Python merge functions; product = merged model weights.
signatures.information: Fixed prompt with one-shot example; dev-set score of merged model; no stronger external model.
signatures.operation: Sample 3000 algorithms/iteration → filter non-executable → merge task vectors into M0 → score on dev → top-3%/bottom-10% DPO pairs (+ replay of earlier top-3) → DPO-train factory → repeat ×3.
signatures.output: Merge functions and merged models; top-15 by dev evaluated once on test.
signatures.conditions: openchat-3.5 seed, three Mistral-7B candidates, math tasks.
signatures.selection_rule: Percentile thresholds on dev score; top-15 by dev for test.
signatures.persistence: Factory weights; merge code reused on new candidates.
signatures.later_use: Next iteration samples from updated factory; algorithms applied to new candidate sets.
signatures.claimed_effect: +6 over seed, +4.3 over Task Arithmetic (GSM8k); +7.4 on transfer.
signatures.failure_boundary: Math only, one model family, seed never fed back, MATH baseline near floor.

gap.checked_gap: Stated limitations of neighbours are specific but not shown binding; the gap concerns weight-level self-improvement, outside the radar's non-weight scope.

gap.closest_adjacent: LLM algorithm discovery without generator training.
gap.residue: Whether training the factory beats sampling more at equal budget is untested.
gap.method_response: Execution-scored preference pairs → DPO on the generator.
gap.remaining_gap: Not evaluated further: out of scope.

reason: Weight boundary: the improver (algorithm factory) is changed by DPO/LoRA weight training and every product of the loop is a new weight vector (merged model). The retained Python merge function is a weight-space operator whose only role is to produce weights; it is not a non-weight harness component (prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator/config) and cannot be plugged into a harness self-improvement loop (not B-class). EVIDENCE.md excludes self-improvement that updates model weights.

resolutions.reason: Scope test applied to the evaluated object, not to the existence of code: (1) the improver is updated by weights (C01, C02); (2) the improved object is weights (C03, C04); (3) the retained code is a merge operator acting on weights, evaluated only through the weights it produces, including in the transfer test (C10). son55's own record concedes the edge (H27 F2 'artifact is a merge operator acting on weights'; unassigned 'weight-space operators lie outside harness-level artifacts'). A trained improver is not disqualifying by itself (H26/H27 in-scope members edit prompts/memory/workflows); the decisive fact is that no non-weight harness artifact is ever changed or retained.
resolutions.score_impact: son55 total 51.25 discarded; paper not scored

resolutions.reason: The authors claim a closed loop (generate → evaluate → DPO → iterate), i.e. a system claim; component_training is for trained components evaluated through an interface. No score effect.

aggregate_review.initial_judgment_before_seat_scores: Factory improved by DPO on its weights; target improved by weight merging; the code artifacts are intermediate weight-update recipes, not harness components → lean out_of_scope, while noting the transfer test does evaluate retained code.
aggregate_review.integrity_checks: Both seats on 2410.15639v5 with matching hashes; seat hashes match conflicts.json.
aggregate_review.core_claim_check: Verified C11/Eq. 6: algorithm A = sequential 0.5·merged + 0.5·mean(next task vector), i.e. ≈0.25·tau_1 plus broadcast means (son55's static reading correct). Seed model never fed back (C05).
aggregate_review.scope_rule_applied: Weight boundary: out of scope when both the improver update and the product are weights, even if code is generated and reused; in scope when a retained non-weight harness artifact is the evaluated object.
